text: libghostty lets anyone build a terminal emulator or embed a terminal into their own applications
quote: Anyone can use `libghostty` to build a terminal emulator or embed a terminal into their own applications.

text: libghostty is a cross-platform, zero-dependency C and Zig library for terminal functionality such as style parsing
quote: `libghostty` is a cross-platform, zero-dependency C and Zig library for building terminal emulators or utilizing terminal functionality (such as style parsing).

text: libghostty-vt is usable today from Zig and C on macOS, Linux, Windows, and WebAssembly
quote: `libghostty-vt` is already available and usable today for Zig and C and is compatible for macOS, Linux, Windows, and WebAssembly.

text: libghostty provides the core terminal emulation, font handling, and rendering
quote: libghostty provides the core terminal emulation, font handling, and rendering capabilities.

text: Reference documentation on terminal concepts and supported control sequences for terminal app developers
quote: For terminal application developers, a reference on terminal concepts and supported control sequences.

text: Supports the Kitty graphics protocol so terminal apps can render images directly in the terminal
quote: Kitty graphics protocol: Ghostty supports the Kitty graphics protocol, which allows terminal applications to render images directly in the terminal.

text: Hundreds of configuration options to customize appearance and behavior
quote: Ghostty supports hundreds of configuration options to make it look and behave exactly how you want.

text: Configuration can be split across multiple files using the config-file key
quote: You can split your configuration into multiple files by using the `config-file` key in your configuration file.

text: Configuration can be reloaded at runtime with a keyboard shortcut
quote: The configuration can be reloaded at runtime by pressing `ctrl+shift+,` (Linux) or `cmd+shift+,` (macOS).

text: Every configuration key can also be passed as a CLI flag when launching Ghostty
quote: Every configuration key is a valid CLI flag when launching Ghostty from the command-line.

text: CLI command shows the default configuration along with its documentation
quote: In the CLI, you can run `ghostty +show-config --default --docs`.

text: Flexible, custom keybindings through the keybind configuration option
quote: Ghostty supports flexible, custom keybindings through the keybind configuration option.

text: Default keybindings differ on macOS and Linux to match each platform's conventions
quote: Ghostty uses different default bindings on macOS and Linux to match the conventions of each platform.

text: Fonts with ligatures render correctly
quote: You can use fonts that have ligatures and Ghostty will render them correctly.

text: Specific font features, such as programming ligatures, can be enabled or disabled
quote: You can use fonts that have ligatures and Ghostty will render them correctly. You can also specify specific font features to enable or disable.

text: Multiple fallback fonts can be configured for codepoints missing from the primary font
quote: This configuration can be repeated multiple times to specify preferred fallback fonts when the requested codepoint is not available in the primary font.

text: Synthetic font styles can be enabled or disabled
quote: Set this to "false" or "true" to disable or enable synthetic styles completely.

text: Embeds a default font (JetBrains Mono) and built-in Nerd Fonts
quote: Ghostty has sensible defaults, embeds a default font (JetBrains Mono), has built-in nerd fonts, and more.

text: Multi-codepoint emoji such as flags and skin tones render correctly as a single character
quote: Multi-codepoint emoji such as flags, skin tones, etc. are rendered correctly as a single character.

text: Quick Terminal: a lightweight terminal that animates down from the menu bar for instant access
quote: Quick Terminal: Lightweight terminal that animates down below the menu bar for instant access without interrupting work.

text: Built-in AppleScript dictionary for scripting windows, tabs, terminals, layouts, and input events
quote: AppleScript Automation: Built-in AppleScript dictionary for scripting windows, tabs, terminals, layouts, and input events.

text: macOS app supports Apple Shortcuts via AppIntents
quote: macOS supports AppleScript, Apple Shortcuts (AppIntents), etc.

text: Secure keyboard entry auto-detects password prompts or can be enabled manually to protect passwords from other processes
quote: Secure Keyboard Entry: Automatically detect password prompts or manually enable secure keyboard entry to protect passwords from other processes.

text: Ships with hundreds of built-in themes, each selectable with a single line of config
quote: Themes: Ghostty ships with hundreds of themes that can be selected with a single line of configuration. Themes can be switched automatically based on system dark/light mode. Users can author their own themes.

text: Themes switch automatically based on system dark/light mode
quote: Themes can be switched automatically based on system dark/light mode.

text: Users can author their own themes
quote: Users can author their own themes.

text: GUI language can be set to something other than the system default
quote: Set Ghostty's graphical user interface language to a language other than the system default language.

text: Works out of the box with zero configuration and sensible defaults
quote: Ghostty is designed to work out of the box with no configuration for most users. Ghostty has sensible defaults, embeds a default font (JetBrains Mono), has built-in nerd fonts, and more.

text: Title bar proxy icon can be dragged to move or access session files, or to navigate to the file path
quote: Proxy Icon: Drag the proxy icon in the title bar to move or access terminal session files, or navigate to the file path directly.

text: macOS Quick Look via three-finger tap or force touch for definitions, web searches, and more
quote: Tap text with three fingers or force touch to use macOS Quick Look for definitions, web searches, and more.

text: Built-in window state recovery on restart on macOS
quote: on macOS, Ghostty supports Quick Look, force touch, the macOS secure input API, built-in window state recovery on restart, etc.

text: Multiple windows, each with its own tabs and splits, rendered with native UI components
quote: Ghostty supports multiple windows, each with its own tabs and splits. These are all rendered using native UI components.

text: Tabs can be renamed and colored
quote: support multi-window, tabbing, and splits with additional features such as tab renaming, coloring, etc.

text: Supports synchronized rendering, which apps like Neovim use to prevent tearing between frames
quote: For example, Neovim uses synchronized rendering to prevent tearing between frames.

text: Linux app integrates with systemd for always-on, single-instance new windows, and cgroup isolation
quote: The Linux app integrates deeply with systemd if available for things like always-on, new windows in a single instance, cgroup isolation, etc.

text: Installable on macOS via a community-maintained Homebrew cask
quote: A Homebrew cask is available and maintained by the Ghostty community. It merely repackages the official `.dmg`

text: Available in the default repositories of many Linux distributions
quote: Ghostty is available in the default repositories for many Linux distributions.

text: Can be tried without installing via nix run or nix-shell
quote: Trying out Ghostty without installing it with `nix run` or `nix-shell` should also work just fine
